title: U.S. House · California's 4th District
area: Covers part of California's North Bay and wine country region, including St. Helena, following the 2025 Proposition 50 mid-decade redistricting.

context.text: The district's boundaries changed as a result of California Proposition 50, approved by voters on November 4, 2025, which redrew the state's congressional map.

Because California uses a top-two primary regardless of party, both general-election candidates are Democrats: Mike Thompson placed first in the June 2, 2026 primary with 41.0% (84,753 votes) and Eric Jones placed second with 22.2% (45,992 votes), ahead of several Republican candidates, out of 206,887 total votes cast.

candidates.name: Mike Thompson
candidates.ballotNote: Placed first in the June 2, 2026 top-two primary
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative (since 2023, prior district); member, House Ways and Means Committee

summary.text: Mike Thompson was born in St. Helena, California, in 1951 and served in the U.S. Army from 1969 to 1972. He served in the California Senate from 1990 to 1998 before being elected to Congress, and serves on the House Ways and Means Committee's Health and Tax subcommittees.

background.text: Graduated from St. Helena High School and served in the U.S. Army from 1969 to 1972.
Earned bachelor's and master's degrees from California State University, Chico, in 1982 and 1996.
Worked as a professor and winery owner; served in the California State Senate from 1990 to 1998 before his election to Congress.
Has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey.

priorities.text: Campaign website cites fiscal responsibility as a priority, calling for a balanced approach to the federal debt that includes spending cuts and higher taxes on those who can afford them, while protecting Social Security and Medicare.
priorities.quote: It is important that we act in a fiscally responsible way while protecting programs like Social Security and Medicare, supporting job creation and also tackling our national debt.

positions.summary: Authored bipartisan legislation requiring criminal background checks for all commercial gun sales.
positions.quote: That’s why I have written and introduced bipartisan legislation that would require comprehensive and enforceable criminal background checks for all commercial gun sales.

positions.summary: Says he is fighting the Medicaid and health coverage cuts in the 2025 budget law, and voted for the Affordable Care Act.
positions.quote: I continue to fight against the healthcare cuts in the Big Ugly Law which kicks 15 million Americans off their healthcare, reversing many of the healthcare coverage gains Democrats have secured.

positions.summary: Says he authored the largest clean energy and energy efficiency climate law and is fighting to restore the clean energy tax provisions the 2025 budget law ended.
positions.quote: The Big Ugly Law ended many of the clean energy tax provisions, and I'm fighting to restore them.

positions.summary: Blames the Administration's tariff war, along with the pandemic, for the high cost of living.
positions.quote: the high cost of living that has been turbocharged by the pandemic and the Administration's tariff war

positions.summary: Says he has supported reform proposals that would increase immigration enforcement while also supporting a pathway to citizenship, protections for DREAMers and a guest worker program.
positions.quote: During my time in Congress, I have supported many immigration reform proposals that would increase immigration enforcement policies, while also supporting policies that would help immigrants who are suffering due to our broken system.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Ways and Means, including its Health and Tax subcommittees, for the 2025-2026 session.
Chaired the Ways and Means Subcommittee on Select Revenue Measures during the 2021-2022 session.

candidates.name: Eric Jones
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary, in which both top finishers were Democrats

summary.text: Eric Jones is a businessman who was a partner at Dragoneer Investment Group before co-founding the Rachel and Eric Jones Foundation and the American Dream Institute, a group focused on youth civic engagement.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from Yale University.

Worked as a partner at Dragoneer Investment Group before leaving to co-found the Rachel and Eric Jones Foundation, described as 'a community-rooted family foundation focused on creating lasting impact across Northern California.'

Co-founded the American Dream Institute, describing it as 'a digital engagement engine built by and for the next generation of voices...founded to raise the voices of young Americans from the ground-up.'

priorities.text: Campaign centers on an 'Affordability Agenda,' proposing a $10,000 middle-class tax credit, holding PG&E accountable for rate increases, lowering prescription drug prices, and expanding Medicare and universal childcare.
priorities.quote: For too many families, the basics of life feel out of reach. Groceries, housing, utilities, health care — everything keeps getting more expensive while wages stay the same.

positions.summary: Campaign platform calls for universal childcare alongside expanded mental health access.
positions.quote: Eric will fight for universal childcare and expanded access to affordable mental health services so families can work.

positions.summary: Supports expanding Medicare to cover dental, vision, hearing aids, and in-home nursing care.
positions.quote: Eric supports expanding Medicare to cover dental, vision, hearing aids, and in-home nursing care.

positions.summary: Platform calls for restoring corporate tax rates and closing zero-tax loopholes, using the revenue to lower costs and reduce taxes for working Americans.
positions.quote: Restore fair corporate tax rates and close the zero-tax loopholes

positions.summary: Platform calls for restoring Congress's constitutional war powers, with no new wars without a congressional vote.
positions.quote: Restore Congress's constitutional war powers : no new wars without a congressional vote

researchNotes: Both general-election candidates are Democrats because of California's top-two primary system. Neither has completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; their stated priorities and positions come from campaign-website text reproduced on their Ballotpedia pages. Jones has held no prior public office.
